Attached: 2 images

Usain Bolt's 9"58 (Berlin 2009) isn't talent, it's a biomechanics study. At 195cm he was "too tall" for sprinting, and his stride is asymmetric: right leg pushes 13% harder than left. He has scoliosis (spine curves, right leg half inch shorter). A "flaw" turned into an edge via near perfect braking propulsion ratio (37%/63%).
Result? Strides up to 2.85m, just 41 steps for 100m, top speed 44.72 km/h
Genetics play a role too, ACTN3 gene (more soon...)
